block.prompt:
SPEAKING — a role-play negotiation in groups of four.

A small town's weekly farmers' market is deciding whether to go COMPLETELY cashless. Each of you takes a role and argues from that person's interests — even if you personally disagree.

• A — a vegetable trader: worried about card fees on every small sale and about machines failing on a busy Saturday.
• B — the town's tourism officer: many visitors are foreign and want to pay by card or phone.
• C — an 80-year-old regular customer: no smartphone, distrusts cards, has always paid in cash.
• D — a young start-up founder: offers a cheap, simple payment app and wants the market to try it.

Discuss, then try to reach ONE joint recommendation the whole group can accept. Write your agreed recommendation in 2–3 sentences on the lines below.
block.answer_key: There is no single correct outcome — the skill is negotiating one workable compromise from clashing interests. A likely joint recommendation: the market stays MIXED for now — every stall must accept both cash and cards, the town helps traders get low-fee card readers, and a paper sign guarantees cash is always welcome so no customer (like C) is excluded. A strong group listens to each role, uses compromise language (“Could we agree that…?”, “As a compromise, …”), and produces a recommendation that visibly takes more than one interest into account. Reward genuine consensus-building over one role simply winning.
block.acceptable_reasoning: Jede Empfehlung ist gültig, sofern sie das Ergebnis echter Aushandlung ist und mehr als ein Interesse berücksichtigt. Bewertet werden Gesprächssteuerung, Kompromisssprache und die Fähigkeit, unterschiedliche Standpunkte zu vergleichen — nicht die konkrete Lösung.

levels: Group genuinely negotiates and reaches a compromise that reflects several interests
A compromise is reached but one or two roles are ignored
One role dominates; no real consensus
Turns managed well; others invited in; comparisons and options offered
Talk overlaps or stalls; little management
Fluent, effective; compromise and comparison phrases used accurately
Limited range that slows the negotiation

watch_outs: Gefahr, dass die stärkste Sprecherin/der stärkste Sprecher die Gruppe dominiert und ‚gewinnt' — Ziel ist Konsens, nicht Sieg. Ggf. jede Rolle zu einem Beitrag verpflichten.
Rollentreue einfordern: C soll aus Sicht der 80-Jährigen argumentieren, auch wenn die Schülerin selbst alles per App zahlt.
Die schriftliche Empfehlung ist nur das Protokoll des Gesprächs — die Sprechleistung ist die eigentliche Aufgabe, nicht das Formulieren der drei Sätze.
Kompromiss-Redemittel oft unbekannt — vorab ein, zwei Wendungen (‚what if we…', ‚as a compromise') an der Tafel bereitstellen.

subject: Lebende Fremdsprache
kompetenzbereich: An Gesprächen teilnehmen und zusammenhängendes Sprechen
